notice: Internal draft for counsel and the owner. It is not an approved legal document, it is not published, and it does not replace the pages now on bizuply.com.

company.formationBasis: The company stated this formation for the draft. The Delaware file number, registered office, and any operating street address were not supplied and are not stated.

privacy.title: Privacy draft
paragraphs: This draft describes personal information handled by Bizuply LLC on the Bizuply platform and on bizuply.com. Bizuply LLC is a limited liability company formed in Delaware, United States. The company serves customers inside and outside the United States. This draft does not treat Bizuply as an Israeli-only company, and it does not apply Israeli law to every customer.

It describes the product as built, including the unreleased consent changes in client PR 1027 and server PR 806. Those changes are not on the public site until they are deployed. The public privacy page remains the page now live on bizuply.com.
A law applies only when its own conditions are met. The general sections apply to the service as operated. The supplements at the end apply only to a person who is actually covered by that law.
information: Contact form: name, phone, email, and message, kept so the enquiry can be answered.

Registration: email and selected plan. Account creation stores a name, email, and password hash. The card number for a platform subscription is collected by Lemon Squeezy, not stored as a card number in the application records described here.
CRM and related tools: the lead, client, appointment, note, and message records a customer enters.
WhatsApp Business API: phone numbers and message content when a business connects that Meta service.

AI: when an AI feature is used and an OpenAI key is configured, the content required for that feature is sent to OpenAI. This draft does not say whether OpenAI uses that content to train a model. That depends on terms that are not in the product repository.

Browser: a language cookie, a sign-in cookie when a session exists, and a measurement-choice cookie. Meta Pixel cookies are written only after measurement is allowed. The public pages that were checked do not load Google Analytics or Google Tag Manager.
Two-factor authentication was not found in the product and is not claimed.
purposes: To provide the account, CRM, website, automation, and WhatsApp tools the customer turns on.
To charge a platform subscription through Lemon Squeezy.
To remember the language and the sign-in session.
To measure Meta leads and conversions only after the person allows measurement.
To send Bizuply marketing email only when a separate marketing choice was stored as accepted.
privacy.bases: Where the GDPR or the UK GDPR applies to a person, the account and the requested service are provided under the contract, and non-essential measurement and Bizuply marketing email rely on the separate consent described below. A documented legitimate-interest assessment is not in the repository, so this draft does not use legitimate interests as a general basis. Where another law requires a notice or a consent, the same screens are the mechanism that exists today. This draft does not say that mechanism satisfies every statute.
records: Measurement choice: a first-party cookie named bizuply_tracking, set to essential or all, for 180 days. The same question is asked in every country. That is a single product control. It is not a statement that every country requires opt-in consent. The choice can be changed from the reset control on the privacy page in the unreleased client. The choice is stored in the browser cookie, not in the application database.

Terms and marketing, after both pull requests are deployed: the updated client sends a consent key only after the server confirms that the record was stored. The record keeps the key, whether it came from registration or the contact form, the email, locale, plan, terms acceptance, marketing acceptance, notice version 2026-11-06, page address, and the database time. Marketing defaults to not accepted. Refusing marketing does not block registration. A failed save stops the new registration or contact flow and the screen does not say the choice was saved. The same key updates one record. An older client that sends no key continues on the previous path, which creates no consent record and is not described as consent.
The current public site does not yet store these terms and marketing records.
recipients: Lemon Squeezy, for platform subscription checkout.
Stripe, for a merchant's own storefront charges when that merchant connects Stripe. This is separate from the platform subscription.
PayPal, for some store-order confirmations. PayPal is not the platform subscription processor.
MongoDB, for the application database. The storage region is not in the repository.
Railway, for application hosting. The region is not in the repository.
OpenAI, for AI features when they are used.
Meta, for the WhatsApp Business API, for ads a business connects, and for the marketing pixel after measurement is allowed.
Google, for fonts on the marketing site.
Twilio, for phone calls when that feature is enabled.
Cloudflare Turnstile, for a bot check when a site key is configured.
privacy.agreements: Signed processing agreements were not in the repository and are not claimed.
privacy.transfers: The providers above can process information outside the person's country. This draft does not say that information stays in the United States or in any other named country, because the storage region is not in the repository. Where the GDPR or the UK GDPR requires a transfer tool, that tool was not verified here.
privacy.retention: A contact enquiry remains a support ticket until an operator deletes it. The product has no self-service account deletion or export. A 30-day retention setting exists only for certain tenant and site-plugin settings, not as a general schedule. No general retention period is stated.
privacy.security: The public site is served over HTTPS. This draft does not claim encryption at rest, a firewall, an intrusion-detection system, or two-factor authentication.
privacy.requests: Access, correction, and deletion requests go to privacy@bizuply.com. The product does not complete them automatically. No binding response time is stated, because none was verified.

supplements.unitedStates: No single federal privacy statute is treated here as covering every user. The Federal Trade Commission Act prohibits deceptive statements about privacy. State laws, including the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the CPRA, apply to a resident only when that statute's own thresholds are met. Those thresholds were not verified, so this draft does not say the California law applies and does not say the company is exempt. If it does apply, a California resident can request to know, correct, and delete personal information, and to opt out of a sale or share. This draft does not say Bizuply sells personal information. Whether the Meta pixel is a sale or a share under California law is a question for counsel.
supplements.eea: The GDPR applies only in the situations it defines, including an offer of services to people in the European Economic Area or monitoring of their behavior. A multilingual website does not by itself decide that question. If the GDPR applies, the person may request access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, and objection, may withdraw consent, and may complain to a supervisory authority. No lead authority and no EU representative are named, because neither was verified.
supplements.uk: The UK GDPR applies only in the situations it defines. If it applies, the rights correspond to the EEA rights above, and a complaint can be made to the Information Commissioner's Office. No UK representative is named, because none was verified.
supplements.israel: The Protection of Privacy Law, 5741-1981, including Amendment 13, can apply to processing that the statute covers. It does not apply to every customer merely because the site is available in Hebrew or because some customers are in Israel. If it applies, access and correction rights under that law, and the direct-mailing rules for a marketing message, are relevant. Bizuply marketing email is sent only when the separate marketing choice was stored as accepted.
supplements.other: The company has not supplied a list of additional countries where the service is specifically directed. A person in another country can write to privacy@bizuply.com. This draft does not recite every national statute.

terms.title: Terms draft
paragraphs: This is a draft contract between the customer and Bizuply LLC, a limited liability company formed in Delaware, United States. The Delaware file number and registered office were not supplied and are not stated. This draft is not published and does not replace the terms now on bizuply.com.

The service is business software: CRM, websites, automations, and WhatsApp tools, as the selected plan describes. A customer who messages its own clients is responsible for those messages and for the legal basis those messages require. The marketing checkbox in Bizuply's own registration or contact form does not authorize the customer's campaigns.
terms.acceptance: The unreleased registration flow asks for acceptance of the terms before continuing. That acceptance is stored only after the server confirms the record. If the save fails, the flow stops and the screen does not say the acceptance was saved. An older client that does not send a consent key continues on the previous path, which does not create this record.
plans: Monthly business plan: 99 US dollars each month.
Yearly business plan: 990 US dollars each year.
CRM-only plan: 49 US dollars each month.
Website plan: 129 US dollars each year.
terms.billing: Platform subscriptions are charged in US dollars by Lemon Squeezy. The subscription renews automatically until the customer cancels in billing. Cancellation stops the next charge. Access remains until the end of the period already paid. Refunds follow the terms that are actually published at the time of purchase. This draft does not add a no-refund rule, and it does not say that a published refund sentence is enforceable against a consumer. No live charge was made to test checkout.
terms.renewalLaws: Automatic-renewal rules differ by market. US state rules, including California's automatic-renewal statute, and consumer rules in the EEA, the United Kingdom, and Israel can require a specific disclosure and a working way to cancel. The unreleased registration screen shows the price, the US-dollar currency, the billing interval, automatic renewal, the effect of cancellation, and that refunds follow the published terms. Whether that disclosure meets each statute is undecided.
terms.governingLaw: Formation in Delaware identifies the company. It does not, by itself, choose the law of this contract or the privacy law of each customer. The public terms now on bizuply.com contain conflicting governing-law clauses. This draft does not select Delaware law, New York law, or any other law. Counsel has to replace those clauses. A customer outside the United States keeps mandatory rights that a contract cannot remove.
terms.liability: The published terms contain limits and waivers. This draft does not repeat them as enforceable. Counsel has to decide what a consumer in each target market can be asked to waive.

accessibility.title: Accessibility draft
checked: On 6 November 2026, Hebrew and English public pages were opened at desktop width and at a 390-pixel width. The language and direction matched the selection, and the checked pages did not show horizontal page overflow.
In the unreleased client, the contact form associates labels with name, phone, email, and message. On the current public site, those labels are visible and are not associated with the inputs.
In the unreleased registration screen, terms and marketing are separate checkboxes. The terms box is required. The marketing box is optional and starts unchecked.
One contrast change was made: amber labels on a light legal sidebar were darkened. A full contrast audit was not done.
In the unreleased client, a measurement dialog is available before a non-essential Meta pixel loads.
accessibility.notChecked: These checks were not a WCAG 2.1 or 2.2 audit, a full screen-reader pass, a review of every customer template, or a review of every language. The public accessibility page currently displays a WCAG 2.1 Level AA claim with check marks. That claim was not established. This draft does not make it.
accessibility.help: A person who needs assistance can email support@bizuply.com. A coordinator's name and phone number were not supplied.
accessibility.laws: The Americans with Disabilities Act and state access laws can apply to some websites in the United States. The European Accessibility Act can apply to consumer services in its scope in the European Union. The UK Equality Act 2010 can apply to services offered to the public in the United Kingdom. Israel's accessibility regulations and Israeli Standard 5568 can apply to a service those rules cover, and a small-business exemption was not calculated. This draft does not decide that any of these laws applies, and it does not claim conformance with any of them.

ownerDecisions: Whether to publish the Delaware file number and registered office.
The countries where the service is specifically directed.
A general retention period, and whether to add self-service deletion and export.
The accessibility coordinator's name and phone.
Whether, after counsel approves a text, it should replace the public pages.
Storage regions and any signed processing agreements, which can be described only after the documents are produced.
counselQuestions: Which governing law and venue should replace the conflicting clauses in the current public terms.
Which privacy laws apply, given where the company is established, where it directs the service, and whether any statutory threshold is met.
Whether a data-protection officer, an EU representative, or a UK representative is required.
Which duties under Israel's Amendment 13 apply, including any registration or exemption.
Whether the Meta pixel is a sale or a share under California law.
Whether the renewal disclosure meets the automatic-renewal rules of each target market.
Which liability limits are enforceable against a consumer.
Whether the ADA, the European Accessibility Act, the UK Equality Act, or Israeli Standard 5568 applies, and what level of conformance each one requires.
